title: Kahana vs Kit (ConvertKit): Inbox for Reach, Hub for Depth
excerpt: Kit (ConvertKit) is email, newsletter, and creator commerce platform (formerly ConvertKit). Kahana is a durable library home for writing you already publish.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Free Newsletter plan: up to 10,000 subscribers with unlimited broadcasts, landing pages, forms, tagging/segmentation, and selling digital products & subscriptions.
Paid Creator/Starter plans from roughly USD 33/month (≈USD 390/year), scaling with subscriber count; unlimited sends, pay for active subscribers.
Claims ≈99.8% delivery rate and ≈30% average open rate (above many industry averages).

strengths.title: Advanced email marketing and automation
strengths.detail: Visual automation builder with triggers, tags, purchases, and custom fields, welcome sequences, sales sequences, and RSS campaigns.

strengths.title: Robust segmentation and tagging
strengths.detail: Segment by opens, clicks, purchases, and attributes for targeted, personalized email.

strengths.title: Built-in monetization tools
strengths.detail: Sell digital products, paid newsletters, recurring subscriptions, and tip jars from native commerce features.

strengths.title: Generous free plan for early growth
strengths.detail: Free up to 10,000 subscribers with broadcasts, landing pages, forms, tagging, and digital product sales.

weaknesses.title: More complex than pure newsletter platforms
weaknesses.detail: Automations, integrations, and monetization can overwhelm writers who just want write-and-send.

weaknesses.title: Less native community feel than Substack
weaknesses.detail: Primarily one-directional email, no built-in commenting or Notes-style social feed; interaction is mostly email replies.

weaknesses.title: Pricing scales with list size
weaknesses.detail: Free plan is generous, but paid plans grow with subscribers, large lists mean meaningful monthly cost.

weaknesses.title: Marketing vs editorial focus
weaknesses.detail: Built to sell products and services; may fit less well than Substack for purely editorial community brands.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Kit (ConvertKit) is email, newsletter, and creator commerce platform (formerly ConvertKit). They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Kit is a creator marketing platform with powerful features to help you optimize your most important asset, your audience. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Kit (ConvertKit) side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Kit (ConvertKit) you can use Newsletters, Memberships, and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. The inbox is the product: essays, archives, and paid subscriptions you already send on a cadence.

Using Kahana with Kit (ConvertKit)

You can use both. Kit (ConvertKit) keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep Kit (ConvertKit) as distribution. Link a Kahana hub or Club as the deep destination: archives, files, and discussion that survive a missed email.
